patches.notes: First patch through the launcher: proves the auto-updater works. Patches download by themselves from here on.

Roads: all 1,370 km of the Tweed's real roads (OpenStreetMap), cut and filled into the terrain. Cracked old bitumen, faded line markings, gravel shoulders, kerbs and footpaths in town, dirt farm tracks, bridges with barriers and piers, grass and moss creeping back in. Creative / survival mode (Esc menu): Forge only in creative. Forge gets Weapons, Car parts, Tools, Survival, World and Nature tabs with ~100 new Poly Haven scans plus four engines (Holden 202, Toyota 22R, Ford 351 Cleveland, Jeep 4.0) with bolt-on alternators. Cars and props left far away no longer fall through the world.
Updater upgrade: lets the launcher download big updates in pieces. If the next update shows a download error, close the game and open it again.
Updater fix: no time limit on big downloads.

Big one. Simulated driving: real engine torque curves, auto and manual boxes, clutch, diffs (open / LSD / locked), raycast suspension with springs, dampers, bump stops and sway bars, Pacejka tyres; you can watch the shocks, springs, leaf packs, wishbones and sway bars work under the car. Engine sounds synthesised for the 202, 22R, 351 Cleveland and Jeep 4.0, with crackle on lift-off and the starter. Zombies (slow, arms out, they hit hard) and scavs (patrol, suspicion, whistle alarm, they shoot back). Ragdolls, limbs and heads come off, blood, run them over. Six period guns (Lee-Enfield, SLR, Colt Python, side-by-side, sawn-off, 870 pump) held in your hands, aim down the sights with right mouse. Garage (Esc menu, creative): build a vehicle from any cab on a ladder chassis, pick engine, box, axles, springs, travel, damping, tyres, add a third axle, save and drive it. Scanned grass up close. Credits page.

Animation overhaul: every character now shares one humanoid skeleton, so 50+ clips play on any body. New rifle animations (idle, walk, run, crouch, reload), body turns to follow where you look after ~70 degrees (35 with a gun up), head and spine look where the camera looks, legs swing toward the way you're walking. Hands properly on the gun in first and third person (right hand on the grip, left under the fore-end). Scopes on the Lee-Enfield (3.5x) and SLR (4x): aim to get a magnified scope window. Five new zombie models with real zombie walks, idles, attacks, bites and a scream when they spot you. 14 scav camps across the map (fire, shelters, barricades, a wreck, loot, a sentry on the gate). Zombies now wander in along the roads, out of sight, instead of fixed spawns.

F9 bug report: grabs a screenshot and the whole game state (where you are, what you're driving or holding, nearby zombies and scavs, settings, frame rate, recent log), pauses, and lets you type what happened. Save it as a zip, or Send it straight to a private GitHub repo for Claude to read.
Fix: keys added in updates (F9 bug report, fire, aim, reload, weapon slots, holster) weren't being registered on installed copies. They are now.
F9 bug report box now sits in the middle of the screen, so the Send button and token box are visible.

Inventory (I): Unturned-style grid with shaped items, worn clothes and bags add pockets, guns load from carried rounds; F opens crates, ammo boxes and other props; MMB carry, RMB throw; B bandage. HUD health and ammo fixed. New PBR ground at real scale, BlendKit lawn, Poly Haven grass clumps everywhere. Water ripple grid fixed. Iron sights measured from each gun (no more rifles in your face), revolver turned the right way round. Mid-air leg pose. Zombies quieter, no more floor-eating attack. Tyres: grip by ground type, slide falloff, tyre pressure, deflection, smoke, rubber marks, screech, dirt spray; Globe mags in the garage. Cars no longer get stuck on corpses.

Roads round the pub and down Tweed Valley Way past the gallery rebuilt with a node road generator from real map data: proper roundabout with a kerbed island, junctions, and the overtaking lane south of the gallery. Inventory items now have pictures that fill their grid shape (rifles long, pistols short). Engine sounds re-recorded from a real engine simulator. Less blue tint on roads and pale ground; matte ground textures.
Fixes the crash on Play from 0.2.11 (a road texture was missing from the build). The game now also starts without the new roads if they ever fail to load.

Zombies now move on the Hollow Walker's animations: walkers that break into a run when close, shamblers with an unsteady drag, and lurchers that charge head-down; they scream when they spot you. The Hollow Walker is a zombie too. Cars: the auto box holds each gear instead of flicking to third in half a second, tyres keep their grip when they spin instead of doing endless burnouts, sharper steering at speed, the handbrake holds a parked car on slopes, and the speedo reads wheel speed. Roundabout grass is finer and matte. New Forge props: two-storey house, servo canopy, blown V8, 426 Hemi, 1979 pickup V8, oil cans, .45 revolver and scoped rifle. F9 reports now say what's under your crosshair and the state of the nearest car.

Two new guns you can find, pick up and fire: a scoped .308 hunting rifle (5-round bolt action, takes 7.62 rounds) and a .45 Magnum revolver (new .45 ammo); they turn up in military crates, ordinary crates and scav camps, and creative mode starts with both. Three new garage engines, each with its own Engine Simulator sound: a Ford 400 V8 out of a '79 pickup, a Chrysler 426 Hemi with its 4-speed, and a blown big-block with twin superchargers (with blower whine). Bridges: the ends of the decks now meet the road at the right height (most were sitting low, some stopped short), and the bridge sides and undersides are no longer drawn near-black. Gun pictures in the inventory now fill their space properly.

The whole map's roads rebuilt with the road generator from OpenStreetMap: proper junctions, roundabouts with kerbed islands, lane markings and the motorway (bridges keep their decks). Wollumbin / Mt Warning and the ranges round the map are now on the skyline, at their real heights; the haze is lighter so you can see them. Servo canopies on the real service stations and old two-storey houses along the streets. Scav camps laid out like someone lives there: a proper wall, seats round the fire, a store, a tip and a workshop. LAN multiplayer: Pause > Multiplayer to host or join a game on your network.

0.3 update, part 1: the world. Towns and farms are full of buildings now (about 20,000, made by a new house generator: Queenslanders, fibro cottages, brick houses, two-storeys, sheds, machinery sheds, dairies, workshops, warehouses), and you can walk into every one. Rooms are furnished for what they are and the cupboards, fridges, wardrobes and shelves have loot that fits the room; loot comes back if you stay away half an hour, and further from town the odd better find turns up. Doors open and close (F); zombies push them open. The Ampol servo is back at the real fuel stations, shop and workshop fitted out. Roads now lie flat on the ground (no more edges catching the wheels) and grass grips like grass. Day and night (an hour a day, 15 minutes of night, more zombies after dark), rain, storms with lightning, morning fog. The game saves itself: the host keeps the world, everyone keeps their own character.

Roads painted into the terrain (no more flicker or grass through the road). Grass density even around you. Step up lips and stairs (no bump at the bottom of Queenslander stairs). Zombies follow you through doorways and up stairs. Windows: open, climb through (Space), shoot out. Roller doors open/shut with F, zombies can't. Board up doors and windows with G (hammer, nails, planks); zombies bash through, pry off with F and a hammer. Pick up chairs, stools, crates and more (middle mouse). Binoculars and torch equip in primary/secondary with their own models; tape a torch to any gun, T toggles it. New loot: tape, hammer, nails, planks. Engine oil sits sideways in the bag. Project cars: rolling chassis and loose bodies at sheds and behind houses. Spanner + K opens the garage on the car in front of you. Car boots/trays hold stuff. Cars you drive are saved. Co-op: no friendly fire. Survival starts without a car. Fixed the invisible wall left by dead zombies.

Shops! Main streets are now rows of shopfronts after Murwillumbah's: tall parapets with the building's name and year (stepped, curved, pediment, flat or 60s box), awnings on tie rods over the footpath, highlight windows, big display windows on tiled stall boards, recessed entries, posted verandahs and balconies on the pubs. Chemists, hardware, grocers, cafes, newsagents, clothes and op shops, sports stores, pubs and banks, each with their own shelves and loot (bandages at the chemist, nails and planks at the hardware, ammo at the sports store, a safe in the bank). Some have a flat upstairs with its own street door. Shop windows can be shot out and climbed through. Shops face the main street, not the lane. Fixed the rail across the top of upstairs stairs. Note: the town layout changed, so cupboards and boarded-up doors start fresh.

full.notes: First Godot build with the launcher built in. Pause menu with graphics settings, Forge mode with phys gun and terrain sculpting, 27 drivable bodies, 52 props, your survivor as a full body, cab view and hop-out fixes.
